newsitem.title: EGYPT: Sudan says Ethiopia attacks, wants mobilisation.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says Ethiopia attacks, wants mobilisation.

text.p: Sudan said on Monday that Ethiopia had attacked two border towns and Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir had called for a general mobilisation.

In a statement read out on state radio, the general command of the Sudanese armed forces said armed forces units stationed in the southeastern towns of Kurmuk and Qeissan, about 600 km (360 miles) south of the capital Khartoum, came under intensive shelling from inside Ethiopia on Sunday.

"At three p.m. (1300 GMT) Ethiopian forces along with some of the remnants of agents and mercenaries launched an attack on the said positions and the fighting continued until seven p.m. (1700 GMT) on Sunday," the statement said.
"The armed forces heroically confronted the enemy and inflicted heavy losses on them," it added.

On Sunday the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) said it had captured Kurmuk and the joint forces of the umbrella opposition group, the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), destroyed four army brigades.

Speaking on state radio, Bashir called on the public and officials "to stand in one rank to preserve the land and faith in response to the enemies of peace and humanity". He called for a "general mobilisation."
The NDA, which includes the SPLA, is fighting to overthrow the Islamist government of Bashir, who took power in a bloodless coup in 1989.
